transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, I’m mostly here because HR and my sister keep saying I’ve gotten too thin. From my side, I don’t know… I just think my suits fit sharper now. But my weight has kept dropping since the divorce, so they wanted me to come in.
Do you think your weight is currently at a healthy level?

I mean… I know everyone’s making a big deal about my weight, but I don’t really see it as unhealthy. I’m still jogging, I’m still working my territory, and I’m hitting my numbers at work, so it doesn’t feel like some kind of medical emergency to me.
Do you think you look too thin when you see yourself in the mirror?

Not really too thin, no. When I look in the mirror, especially before a meeting or if I’m going on a date, I notice my stomach and my face more than anything. If I think I look soft, I start feeling like people are going to see me as sloppy or weak.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah… I guess I am. Like, if I go to a client dinner or spend a weekend out in Miami and the scale is even a pound higher after, I get this panic feeling. It’s like I’m losing control, and I immediately start thinking about how I’m going to cut back the next day.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that you consider excessive in a short period of time?
I don’t think so. I mean, I might eat more than I planned at a dinner or something, but I wouldn’t call it excessive. I’m usually pretty aware of what I’m eating.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives after eating?
No, I don’t make myself throw up. And I don’t use laxatives after eating either.
Do you exercise to burn off calories or prevent weight gain?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do exercise sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s specifically to burn off calories or stop weight gain. It depends.
Have you had any periods in the past where you gained a significant amount of weight?
Not really, no. I can’t think of a time where I gained a significant amount of weight. Maybe small changes here and there, but nothing major that I’ve noticed.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while you're eating?
I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t really have times where I feel out of control eating. I’m usually pretty aware of what I’m doing.
When you think about your weight or body shape, do you think it's different from how other people see you?

Yeah, I think it might be. Like before a meeting or a date, I’ll look in the mirror and I kind of fixate on my stomach or my face. If I think I look soft, I assume other people are going to see that too, like I look sloppy or weak. I don’t know if they actually see me that way, but that’s where my mind goes.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is related to how you want to look or how you think others see you?

Yeah, I think so. It’s tied to how I look and how I think people are judging me. Like if the scale is even a pound higher after a client dinner or a weekend out, I get this panic feeling, like I’m losing control. Then I start thinking about how I’m going to cut back the next day.
Do you find yourself thinking about your weight or body shape at times when you're not trying to think about it?

Yeah. It kind of pops up even when I’m not trying to think about it, especially before something like a meeting or a date. I’ll catch myself checking the mirror and then I just zero in on my stomach or my face. If I think I look soft, I start assuming people are going to see me as sloppy or weak.
Has your concern about your weight or body shape interfered with your relationships or work in any way?

Yeah, it has. I still get my sales route done and I’m functioning at work, but I’ve been avoiding client dinners unless I know I can control what I’m eating. Same with dating, honestly. If I don’t know the menu or feel like I can’t manage it, I’ll just turn it down. So I’ve been keeping to myself more than I used to.
When you look at yourself, do you see yourself as being underweight, even if others might say you are?

Not really. I mean, I know people are making a big deal about my weight, but I don’t look at myself and think, like, “I’m dangerously underweight.” I’m still jogging, still working my territory, still hitting my numbers, so it just doesn’t feel like some medical emergency to me.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the most important part of how attractive you are to others?

Yeah, I think it matters a lot to me. Like before a meeting or a date, I’ll look in the mirror and I go straight to my stomach or my face. If I think I look soft, then I start feeling like other people are going to see me as sloppy or weak.
Are there any social activities that you've stopped doing altogether because of your concerns about weight or body shape?

Yeah. I mean, I haven’t stopped everything, but I’ve pretty much stopped doing client dinners or going on dates if I don’t know the menu or can’t control what I’m eating. I still do my sales route and get my work done, but I turn down a lot of invitations now, so I’m definitely keeping to myself more.
When you look at yourself, do you think there's a difference between how you see your body and how it actually is?

Yeah, I guess there probably is. Like, before a meeting or a date, I’ll look in the mirror and I don’t really see the whole picture—I go straight to my stomach or my face. If I think I look even a little soft, it feels obvious to me, like everyone else is going to notice and think I look sloppy or weak.
Was there something specific that happened, like a comment or an event, that made you start worrying about gaining weight?

I don’t know if there was one specific comment or event. It’s more like, if I go to a client dinner or have a weekend out in Miami and the scale is even a pound higher after, I panic. It feels like I’m losing control, and then I immediately start planning how I’m going to cut back the next day.
Do you think your perception of your own body shape or weight is accurate?

Honestly, probably not. I think I get really focused on certain parts, like my stomach or my face, especially before a meeting or a date. If I think I look even a little soft, it feels like everyone else is going to notice and see me as sloppy or weak. So... yeah, I don’t think I’m seeing it accurately all the time.
Do you think you would still worry about your weight if everyone around you told you that you look healthy and normal?

Yeah, I think I still would. Even if everyone said I looked healthy or normal, if I got on the scale after a client dinner or a weekend away and it was even a pound higher, I’d panic. It feels like I’m losing control, and then I start thinking right away about how I’m going to cut back the next day.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent fear of gaining weight, distorted body image, and excessive self-evaluation of body shape and weight, despite being underweight, are characteristic of an eating disorder. However, the patient does not exhibit behaviors typical of anorexia nervosa, such as restrictive eating or binge-purging behaviors, which are necessary for a diagnosis of F50.0. Instead, the patient's symptoms align more closely with body dysmorphic disorder (F40.9), which is characterized by a preoccupation with a perceived flaw in appearance, in this case, the patient's weight and body shape.
